The store measures lease and window expiry on Redis's server clock rather than the client's clock.
A slot acquired on a short lease becomes admissible again once that lease's duration has elapsed on Redis's clock.
A request or cost window entry remains counted against a 60 second window and is judged against a 0.3 second window only by the store's own time comparison.
The store prunes expired window entries itself, so a key's TTL covering the full window does not remove live entries early.

Reading Redis's clock before and after an acquire yields timestamps that bracket the lease's start time.

The target repository has auto-merge allowed in its settings, and the token has permissions sufficient to enable it.

assumptions.target: gh CLI authentication and GitHub token

The file exists but is intentionally not used as evidence for served models or row identity.

The image tag v0.28.59 resolves to an image digest that the action-pin catalogs can record as immutable.

The handler currently applies patch and bundle artifacts from disk without binding them to the bytes that were validated.

The Model Routing page's previous content contained AWF internals, log paths and version tables that are being removed in favour of an author-focused page.
The routing implementation has been checked and the new Model Routing page's statements match its current behaviour without requiring factual corrections.
The allowed-models setting accepts exact model names only and does not accept patterns, which belong in models.allowed and models.blocked.

The GitHub provider is selected when model-provider is github or the model string has a copilot/ prefix, and the Anthropic provider output must remain unchanged.
A user-supplied --settings argument in engine.args or safe-outputs.threat-detection.engine.args is preserved verbatim, and the compiler only emits a warning rather than merging in the generated map.
The smoke-claude-on-copilot workflow is an existing test that currently fails deterministically on every run and is expected to pass once the overrides are applied.
The control variant currently performs open-ended module research that includes browsing issues and discussions, which drives high AI request counts.

The experiment flag is supplied at runtime with the value "candidate" or another variant string so the handlebars conditional selects the correct branch.

The completeness eval and request-count and tool-failure graders can be added and will run against the 20 samples per variant with Mann-Whitney analysis.
Current control runs achieve completeness high enough that a 90% threshold is a meaningful comparison point.

Parsing and config building preserve a nil AllowedModels value through to the emitted apiProxy.routing.candidateModels field so omission is observable.
The field is omitted from generated config when no shortlist applies, and is a list of provider-qualified model names when one does.
When the main workflow has no routing settings, the first import's routing settings are copied into the result unchanged.

The table-driven test exercises every combination of main and imported allowed-models presence through ParseWorkflowFile and BuildAWFConfigJSON.
The compiler package in pkg/workflow builds and runs with the existing Go toolchain without additional dependencies introduced by this change.

The root go.mod file declares the repository's minimum required Go version and is readable by setup-go's go-version-file input.
The checkout step runs before Go setup, so the root go.mod is present in the workspace when setup-go reads it.

assumptions.claim: Removing aw_context preserves all other workflow_dispatch inputs and surrounding comments in the file.
Workflows declare the engine via engine.id, which identifies whether a workflow is a Copilot CLI, Copilot SDK, or other-engine workflow.
Existing codemod tests exercise the fix pipeline so new Copilot web-fetch and aw_context fixers can be verified against them.
The base.sha reported by the pulls.get API can be a stale merge base already contained in the old PR head rather than the current base branch tip.

The 294 PR-branch handler tests, including real-Git ancestry scenarios and missing or empty base-ref fallbacks, pass on the changed code.
The GitHub API exposes separate core, code_search, and search rate-limit buckets with limit, remaining, and reset values that can be read before and after agent execution.

Failed MCP responses carry retry hints (such as Retry-After) that are currently not surfaced in gateway or RPC logs.

Legacy summary entries use a pipe-delimited format of source, tool, and retry message that existing parsers accept with the added retry text.
The checkout action supports cross-repository checkout with authentication and sparse-checkout for local code searches.

assumptions.claim: Existing logging tests pass unchanged after the new quota snapshot and 429 diagnostic output is added.
The add_comment tool currently enforces a fixed 50-URL limit on comment content.
Generated footer and metadata links are appended to the comment body during posting, after the tool-level link check has run.

Workflow permission checks run during test execution and do not depend on sandbox tool availability.

Adding model.inventory to the interpreted event types is sufficient to route inventory events through the foreign-engine evidence check.

The release v0.28.57 of gh-aw-firewall exists and is available to pin.
The release v0.4.31 of gh-aw-mcpg exists and is available to pin.

These outputs currently present credit figures in a form that can be extended to show recorded, estimated, and combined credits separately.

Successor Work remains blocked until the Work reaches terminal completion, and the Work's payload, effect contract, resource scope, scheduling entitlement, and worker profile are preserved across keep-open continuations.
Both create_pull_request and push_to_pull_request_branch exist as the intended final code-delivery paths for long-running work.

Pricing a marked read of a background response at zero is the mechanism that prevents double billing across reads and polls.
An unmarked read of a background response is the only place its spend is recorded in the SDK and in proxies without a database.
A create that sends background in extra_body or that the provider reports as background is stored as a row whose status is queued or in_progress until it is claimed.
The background poll bills a response once and does not run under any key, so its charge must be attributed from the stored row.
Moving a stored row out of queued or in_progress with one conditional update guarantees that only one reader or poller bills the response.

Callback writes to S3 and GCS run in the background so that a slow or failing bucket does not block or delay billing.
Each line record contains the request, the response or error, token counts, cost and the batch creator's identity.

The Add Model form accepts prefilled parameters and can create models for the providers listed as supported by this build.
The Models page lets an admin add models only when the admin is not view-only, and that permission check is available to the AI Hub.
This proxy build exposes its own list of decision providers that it can serve on /v1/decisions, and the AI Hub can compare cost map providers against it.
The docs site has a self-hosted section for Laya and Nimble and a note on deploying Microsoft Foundry under your own name, and these anchors exist for the cards to link to.

assumptions.target: fine_tuning create, retrieve and cancel endpoints
assumptions.claim: The proxy forwards fine-tuning create, retrieve and cancel requests to the provider and returns the provider's job response.
Create forwards validation_file, hyperparameters, suffix and seed to the provider unchanged, along with model and training_file.
The unversioned /fine_tuning/jobs routes are currently mapped and route to the same handlers as the versioned endpoints.

assumptions.target: Azure finetune_settings credentials on create and cancel
assumptions.claim: Azure create and cancel requests carry finetune_settings credentials and the prompt_loss_weight and trainingType fields to the provider.
With require_managed_files enabled, raw provider file and job IDs are refused in training_file, validation_file and job ID positions.

assumptions.target: managed file and job ownership across API keys
assumptions.claim: Managed training files, validation files and jobs are owned by the key that created them, and other keys are refused access to them in both proxy modes.
The provider's fine-tuning job response contains every field the OpenAI SDK reads and conforms to a strict Job model with no extra fields.
The scripted upstream drains its queued responses fully within each test and records the exact provider request for assertion.
PluginSpec currently has no installation_preference field, so adding it as an optional field is a new addition rather than a replacement.
Generated marketplace.json plugin entries currently contain only name, source and version and never include any installation-related key.
Claude Desktop reads installationPreference per plugin in marketplace.json and treats same-origin plugins as manual install when the key is absent.
A plugin source of type archive carries a url and an sha256 field, and a github source type exists as a distinct source variant.
POST, PUT, list, detail and skill hub responses for plugins currently do not include an installation preference field, so echoing it is a new response shape.
The existing plugin API returns 422 for invalid field values and 400 for invalid source and field combinations, consistent with the codes used elsewhere in this endpoint.
Existing plugin creation and marketplace.json generation tests pass before this change and do not assert on the absence of installationPreference.
The proxy serves marketplace.json from the same origin as the plugin endpoints, so Claude Desktop pointed at that origin reads the emitted file.
The /key/block endpoint refuses a warm key with 401 auth_error on both gateway and peer workers before any upstream call is made.
The /key/unblock endpoint restores serving of a previously blocked key on both workers.
The /key/info endpoint reports a blocked key as blocked after a block call.
The Postgres VerificationToken row for a blocked key reflects blocked status after the block call.
Key revocation and rotation routes evict cached key state on every worker so a stale cached key is not served.
The integration test harness can run a gateway and a warmed peer worker against a scripted upstream and a Postgres database.
The /jwt/key/mapping/update endpoint changes the key mapping used by subsequent JWT requests on all workers.
The proxy endpoint POST /customer/new accepts a max_budget field and creates a customer that enforces that budget.

A chat completion naming a customer via body user, x-litellm-end-user-id, x-litellm-customer-id, litellm_metadata.user, metadata.user_id, or Responses safety_identifier is refused with 422 budget_exceeded once that customer's spend reaches its budget.
Deleting a user, SCIM user, or organization causes the proxy to refuse that user's or org's keys on the next gateway call, including on a warmed peer instance with cached auth.
A successful request to a customer-scoped key writes rows to the spend and daily spend tables that can be read back from the database.
The owned upstream receives the request body unchanged enough that it can be asserted in full by the test.
The integration test harness can start the real proxy and an owned upstream server and run them against a database in CI.
The test suite provides a controllable upstream stub that records each incoming request for inspection.
The integration test runner accepts suite names like providers and extensions and runs the listed test files against a locally started proxy on port 4000.
The integration rig provides Postgres and Redis locally with no ambient provider API keys set, so tests run against the scripted upstream only.
Redis 8 running locally is compatible with the integration tests even though CI uses Redis 7.

assumptions.target: Assistants, threads, and Evals proxy routes
assumptions.claim: Several Assistants, threads, and Evals routes are currently broken on main for real SDK request spellings, so their tests skip with a BUG marker rather than fail.
The scripted upstream server returns canned responses that match the wire contracts the new tests assert against.
The existing skipped tests in this file are the only tests covering the eight identified gaps, and no other test in the repo exercises these routes through the proxy.
Merging origin/main into this branch does not change the set of routes under test, so the pass and skip counts from before the merge remain meaningful after it.
The proxy forwards requests to the upstream over HTTP and the tests observe the exact wire request the upstream receives.
The proxy replaces the caller's virtual key with the real proxy x-api-key before forwarding, and merges the caller anthropic-beta header with the credential beta value.
The proxy forwards multipart form bodies unchanged, preserving repeated image[] parts, mask, string-typed n and stream fields, and file and text parts.
The proxy strips the caller credential (x-goog-api-key or ?key=) and forwards only the proxy key, keeping alt=sse and the request body unchanged.
Both aliases route to the same regional or global Vertex upstream host and attach a minted bearer token, adding alt=sse when the caller omits it.
The google-genai SDK sends x-goog-api-key and alt=sse headers and v1beta1 paths that the proxy accepts.
The Anthropic SDK and AnthropicVertex client send requests in the spellings the proxy's pass-through routes expect.
Each new integration test has been mutation-proven, meaning a one-line product change causes it to fail and the change was reverted.
The proxy serves MCP at the per-server path /mcp/{alias} and scopes tool listing and tools/call to only that server.
The proxy accepts comma-separated server aliases in the /mcp path, with an optional trailing segment, and scopes tools to exactly the listed servers.
The legacy /{name}/mcp form resolves comma lists with whitespace and duplicates, access-group tags, and toolset names to the correct set of servers.

assumptions.target: unknown server alias in comma list
assumptions.claim: A comma list containing only unknown aliases returns HTTP 404 before any request is sent to an upstream peer.
A tools/call on a server outside the requested path is refused without sending anything to that server, and tool calls reach only the target peer with the unprefixed tool name and verbatim arguments.
Authorization code redemption and refresh at /{alias}/token and root /token reach the upstream IdP with the expected client_id and grant parameters.
The official MCP SDK streamable HTTP client is compatible with the proxy's session id, notifications/initialized, and protocol header handling.
The scripted upstream peer, mock IdP and Postgres test fixtures exist and are available to run the integration suite.
The endpoint accepts general_settings, litellm_settings, environment_variables and router_settings in a single body and persists them to Postgres and the runtime without wiping sibling settings.
Re-posting a plugin config with its key shown as *** keeps the stored key unchanged rather than overwriting it with the mask.
Deleting a callback by callback_name removes it from the live success_callback list so prompts no longer reach that sink.
The endpoint saves Vault configuration with AppRole and TLS cert auth and reads back token values masked.
Stored Vault tokens are masked in HTTP responses and are encrypted at rest in Postgres.
Config changes and deletions propagate to every worker so the deleted callback is inactive on all workers.
AppRole and cert logins to Vault are performed within the configured login namespace.
Each of the 9 integration tests fails when a one-line regression is introduced under litellm/, so they detect the regressions they target.
The /budget/update endpoint accepts a tier's max_budget change and returns 200 on success.
Keys on a budget tier are re-evaluated against the updated max_budget within the key cache window after a /budget/update call.
Requests on a key whose spend exceeds a lowered tier max_budget are refused with a budget_exceeded error naming the new max budget.
The /key/spend/report endpoint returns 403 with a fixed body when an internal user requests another user's api_key.
The spend log table in Postgres holds the rows whose SUM equals the own-scope totals returned by the spend report.
The scripted upstream records every request that reaches it, including method, path, authorization and body, so a refused call can be shown to make no provider request.
A Postgres instance is available to the integration test run as the backing store for spend and budget data.
A real litellm proxy is started in the test environment pointed at the scripted upstream and the Postgres instance.
The test exists and verifies that an unmanaged response ID is forwarded to the upstream vendor unchanged on create.
The streamed-ID test retrieves the streamed response ID, compares the full response, and checks the exact upstream GET request.
Integration tests run against a real local proxy backed by a scripted upstream, so exact request and response contracts can be asserted.
The /debug/memory/summary endpoint reports a worker_pid for each proxy worker.
The /model/info endpoint reports the deployment served by each worker when queried on the same connection as /debug/memory/summary.
Readiness is reached only when every worker reports the deployment, so tests registering Cursor and compact routes can safely run after readiness.
The test files covering Cursor and compact routes pass with 38 passed tests and 5 BUG skips at the referenced commits.
The proxy enforces Responses ownership and previous-response affinity so tests can assert those behaviours across supported route aliases.
The proxy exposes an Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint that accepts the Claude Code CLI spelling including the ?beta=true query parameter.
The proxy forwards the client's comma-separated anthropic-beta tokens upstream exactly, neither dropping nor adding any tokens, including unknown future betas.
For native Anthropic deployments the proxy returns the upstream JSON body unchanged to the client, including fields such as safeguard_results.
Upstream 429, 400 and 529 errors are surfaced to the client as Anthropic error envelopes with matching status codes and SDK exception classes.
When the upstream stream errors mid-response, the client receives message_start followed by an error event and no message_stop event.

assumptions.target: Vertex and Azure AI Claude branches
assumptions.claim: Requests routed to Vertex AI and Azure AI Claude deployments follow the same request and response contracts as the native Anthropic path.
The six known current-main product bugs are pinned as BUG-marked skipped tests whose bodies describe the correct expected behaviour.
The proxy accepts repeated target_model_names[] multipart parts on the files upload endpoint and forwards them to the provider.
The batches cancel endpoint enforces tenant ownership and returns 403 when the caller's key does not own the managed batch.
The managed file record stores the list of target model names for each uploaded file.
Managed file ids encode the target model so the proxy can route follow-up requests to the correct deployment.
The proxy currently reads repeated target_model_names[] fields without collapsing them to a single value.
This test file is new and runs with a scripted provider against the real proxy on every merge.
The OpenAI SDK sends extra_body fields as repeated target_model_names[] multipart parts on file upload.
Streaming responses currently drop the upstream usage object when the final usage chunk also contains a choices array.
Provider SDK usage objects carry a cached_tokens field that can be mapped onto litellm's Usage on ingest.
Cost for streamed requests is currently billed at the full input rate because cached_tokens is lost.
litellm's Usage type is the normalized usage representation that ingested provider usage objects can be converted into.
The model config supplies cache_read_input_token_cost alongside input and output token costs so cached tokens can be priced differently.
Existing streaming tests pass and the newly added tests cover a usage chunk that also carries choices.

The proxy's chat completions endpoint reroutes to context_window_fallbacks or content_policy_fallbacks only when the upstream returns the matching OpenAI 400 error code, and uses general fallbacks for other failures such as a plain 500.
A request carrying disable_fallbacks returns the upstream error as a literal 400 and never invokes any fallback model.
The proxy reports the fallback attempts it made in the x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks response header.
When a stream fails before or after the first event, or stream is false, the proxy falls back and the client receives exactly one well-formed SSE stream.
Spend for a fallen-back request is recorded against the fallback group rather than the original primary model.
For a non-admin key, GET /health returns 403 when asked for another team's public name or model_id and does not probe that team's upstream.
When both model_id and model are supplied, model_id takes precedence and access groups expand to their member deployments.
Each mock_testing flag forces its own fallback chain to run without calling the primary deployment.
The new crate litellm-llms-types is created as part of this change and is available to the workspace for consumers to depend on.
Shared inference models (chat, messages, responses, embeddings, OCR) currently live in a legacy shared types crate that spans multiple crate boundaries.
Chat, messages, responses, embeddings, and OCR format contracts can be imported from the format module namespace of litellm-llms-types.
Provider-specific wire contracts can be imported from the provider module namespace of litellm-llms-types.
Workspace compilation validates all updated downstream consumers together after the move to litellm-llms-types.
The handful of test files covering this change pass locally at commit 5372ac7917.
RedisCache already exposes or will gain an async_publish method that other proxy components can call to publish messages to Redis channels.
RedisCache can open a shared pub/sub subscription via async_subscribe returning a RedisSubscription, usable by config sync and auth invalidation.
Under a Redis Cluster client, some pub/sub and lock paths are silently disabled, so cross-worker coordination degrades rather than failing loudly.

assumptions.target: proxy helpers (config sync, auth invalidation, credential refresh lock)
assumptions.claim: These helpers currently reach directly into the raw redis client for pub/sub and locking rather than going through a shared cache surface.
Debug stats can read Redis connection pool state through RedisCache.connection_pool_status instead of accessing the raw client.
The litellm-rust crate's cache backend abstraction is able to host a new PubSubCache capability trait and a Redis implementation of it.
The proxy runs with a Redis cache backend shared across multiple worker processes so that cross-worker coordination is required.
The banner currently has a dismiss (X) control that hides it for the user's browser, introduced by PR #40831.
Environment-credential login via UI_USERNAME and UI_PASSWORD still works while the banner is shown.
Setting general_settings.disable_env_credential_login to true is the only supported way to clear the env-credential login warning banner.
Reverting commit c1aaaae4e3 with git revert -m 1 cleanly restores the non-dismissible banner without requiring any other changes.
The test files covering the banner change pass locally and are sufficient to validate the revert.
The crate litellm-accounting exists and exposes a per-call settlement state machine over backend effects that the PR builds on.
The gateway-inference crate can host an accounting module that is wired to the /responses endpoint through native call interceptors.
The host currently lacks a serve_with_hooks entrypoint, and existing serve entrypoints remain unchanged by its addition.
The /v1/responses endpoint currently executes requests without any budget reconciliation, spend recording, or reservation release.
Monetary settlement for calls is currently owned by Python, with no equivalent settlement path in native Rust calls.
Native call interceptors are awaited by the host, so an accounting failure can be surfaced before the response is returned.
The deployment can inject an AccountingService at startup to be used by the /v1/responses handler.
The PR includes meaningful tests covering the new accounting behaviour, although the test files covering the change are not all listed yet.
mocked_group registers one model group over mock_response deployments and a key pool with zero provider spend, and ResourceManager tears it down afterwards.
measure runs Locust through a discarded warm-up phase followed by a kept measured phase.
The gateway exposes a /debug/memory/summary endpoint reporting per-worker RSS, readable before and after the load run.
When pods are replaced mid-load, new workers are compared against the median old worker, so a rolling upgrade alone does not trip the RSS growth ceiling.
problems returns the list of broken budgets (failures, Locust saturation, rps floor, p50/p90/p99 ceilings, worst-worker RSS growth) and the test asserts that list is empty.
Six mocked deployments (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock converse, Vertex AI, Gemini) each respond after a mock_delay within 0.5 to 2.0 seconds.
The router spreads requests across the six deployments so the gateway holds requests while waiting on slower responses.
Adding a user who already has a membership row for the team currently fails with a 500 Unique constraint error on (user_id, team_id) instead of succeeding.
Concurrent first-use adds of the same user to the same team can both reach the membership insert after the lock, so the insert itself is not protected against races.
A membership row for (user_id, team_id) can exist while the corresponding team roster entry is missing, and the desync is not repaired automatically.
Each failed add attempt currently clones an extra per-member budget row before the insert fails.
A lookup of the existing membership row by user_id and team_id is available and can be performed before the budget is resolved.
The caller re-appends the missing roster entry when an existing membership is returned, which is what heals users wedged by the desync.
The model identifier openai/gpt-5.6-terra is a valid, routable model name on the OpenAI provider in LiteLLM.
The model identifier azure/gpt-5.6-terra is a valid, routable deployment name on the Azure provider in LiteLLM.
gpt-5.6-terra is a tier 1 GPT model that currently has no translation test coverage in the suite.
The proxy serves the chat_completions, messages and responses endpoints for the openai and azure routes with gpt-5.6-terra as the model.
The base case request and response bodies were captured from the real OpenAI and Azure providers and are accurate representations of their wire format.
A fake provider deployment is listening on 127.0.0.1:8191 and can be configured to serve the openai and azure gpt-5.6-terra routes.
The integration suite runs case-by-case assertions on upstream request bodies and client-facing replies, so new cases will be executed alongside existing ones.
Before this change, the Purview guardrail always requests its token from the commercial Entra authority and calls the commercial Graph endpoint regardless of AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST.

Before this change, Microsoft SSO default authorize, token, userinfo and group lookup URLs are hardcoded to the commercial cloud and ignore AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST, so operators must set three full URL overrides.
The new module exposes an authority normalizer and per-cloud Graph and Monitor audience lookups that can be called from Purview, Microsoft SSO, Sentinel and the Azure OIDC token exchange.

assumptions.target: Sentinel logger authority normalization and cloud lookup
assumptions.claim: The authority normalization and cloud lookup logic currently lives only in the Sentinel logger and can be moved out without changing its observable behaviour.

Operators set AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST to the authority of their cloud (for example https://login.microsoftonline.us for Azure Government) and this value is the source of truth for all Azure authority-derived endpoints.
A default Azure authority host constant is defined in litellm/constants.py and is used when AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST is unset.
Each sovereign cloud has a matching Graph base URL and scope (for example graph.microsoft.us for Azure Government) that corresponds to its Entra authority host.
The /v1/decisions endpoint currently rejects requests containing input_image content parts with a 400 error.
The /v1/systemone endpoint currently accepts an images field but silently drops it before reaching Cloudflare Clef.
Cloudflare Clef accepts up to 4 images per request in an images field.
A provider capability flag named supports_image_input exists and gates whether image input is forwarded or refused.
Non-Cloudflare System One providers currently refuse image requests rather than silently dropping images.
The images field accepts either data URLs or objects with content_type and base64 keys.

assumptions.target: MCP tool calls, prompts/get and resources/read
assumptions.claim: Before this change, calls to MCP servers were not checked against any data boundary and a cross-boundary call succeeded with HTTP 200.

assumptions.target: keys and teams without an allowlist
assumptions.claim: Keys and teams with no mcp_data_boundaries allowlist continue to reach every MCP server exactly as they did before this change.
MCP server records have no existing data boundary or residency field, so a new data_boundary label can be added to them.
Key and team object permissions have a permissions structure that can hold a new mcp_data_boundaries allowlist.
The MCP REST tools/call endpoint is the request path that must enforce the boundary check and return a 403 on violation.
MCP servers can be declared in config with a data_boundary key that the proxy reads at startup.
The admin UI at /ui/?page=mcp-servers exists and exposes fields for setting a server's data boundary and a key or team's allowed boundaries.
The MCP REST gateway exposes a tools/call endpoint that forwards tool invocations to the upstream MCP server and returns the upstream result.

assumptions.target: delete_record tool call without approval header
assumptions.claim: Currently the gateway forwards a delete_record call with no approval header and returns HTTP 200, so high-risk tools are callable without any sign-off.
Currently any approval-like header supplied by the client is forwarded unchanged to the upstream server and to pre_mcp_call hooks without validation.

assumptions.target: request log for MCP tool calls
assumptions.claim: Currently the request log records MCP tool calls but contains no information about who approved a call.
The external approval service publishes a JWKS document at the configured URL from which signing keys for approval JWTs can be fetched.
MCP server configuration accepts an approval_policy setting, and servers without this setting keep their existing behaviour with no approval check.
The gateway has a JWT library capable of verifying RS/ES-signed tokens against keys retrieved from a JWKS URL.
The admin UI Settings tab for an MCP server exists and can be extended with an Approval references form.
Request kwargs are not forwarded upstream to Vertex, so a caller-supplied vertex_ai_cache_creation_input_tokens field never reaches the provider.
The cache creation token count is stored on the Logging object and is not read from request kwargs, so callers cannot set it.
The cachedContents response from Vertex is the trusted source of cache creation token counts, and it may contain negative values that must be clamped to 0.
The old VERTEX_AI_CACHE_CREATION_TOKENS_KEY constant is still in use by the code this PR removes it from, so removal is safe once the Logging attribute is used instead.
Prompt token and cost calculations for vertex_ai/* models currently derive cache creation usage from request kwargs, which is what makes negative spend possible.
The test files covering the cache creation token path exist and pass locally with the change applied.
The README header contains an Enterprise Tier link written as an HTML anchor tag that includes a target="_blank" attribute.
The missing space before target="_blank" currently causes the anchor attribute to be malformed or not parsed correctly.
The Databricks supported params list does not currently include service_tier, so it is dropped from outgoing requests.
The Responses API bridge currently ignores service_tier present in the request body.
Streamed responses currently lose the service_tier returned by Databricks in the stream wrapper and during aggregation.
Databricks priority-tier traffic is currently priced at standard rates, so spend is under-counted.
A returned service_tier of default currently overrides a requested priority tier during cost calculation.
The integration test fails when _resolve_service_tier returns None, demonstrating that priority requests are forwarded and charged at priority rates once the fix is applied.
The Vertex AI cachedContents response is retained in full rather than only its name and model fields, so creation time and expiry time are available to downstream code.
Vertex Gemini creates cache entries automatically for prompts carrying cache_control, and the creation step is currently not billed as cache_creation_input_tokens.
A helper named _add_cache_creation_usage exists in the vertex_ai code path and adds creation tokens to usage on the request that creates the cache.
generic_cost_per_token decides the above-128k pricing tier from the generateContent prompt, counting text plus cache reads.
Response _hidden_params is carried into the standard logging payload, so cached content name, create time and expire time reach spend callbacks.
The integration test exists and fails when _add_cache_creation_usage is removed, verifying cache creation and read tokens are charged in SpendLogs.
The Vertex AI Gemini API supports cachedContents resources with name, create time and expire time fields in its responses.
The function currently enforces a 30-second wall-clock deadline on schema validation of tool arguments.
The test currently pins the process to a single CPU core and expects 8 cold workers to start within 30 seconds.
The test fails intermittently (about a quarter of mcp-server runs on main) because of the wall-clock deadline rather than because of a validation defect.
The function accepts a keyword-only timeout_seconds parameter that can be set to math.inf to disable the deadline.
This integration test exists and independently verifies that the 30-second deadline stops expensive validation work and that the system recovers.
Production callers do not pass timeout_seconds and therefore continue to receive the 30-second default limit.
Without defer_index_build, the proxy embeds all MCP tools synchronously before binding the port when the semantic tool filter is enabled.
The defer_index_build setting defaults to false, so existing deployments keep the current blocking index build behaviour.

assumptions.target: MCP tool requests during index build
assumptions.claim: While the background index is not yet ready, requests receive the full unfiltered tool list rather than an error.
The periodic DB settings sync rebuilds the semantic tool index on every tick unless a background build has already run.
The semantic tool filter can be enabled from config.yaml, the settings API, or the Admin UI Semantic Filter tab.
The configured embedding model enforces a context window that build-time tool descriptions can exceed, producing a 400 error.
The deployment's liveness probe is set to 90 seconds and restarts the pod when the health endpoint is unreachable for that period.
The uv tool is available on the Windows CircleCI executor so it can be installed before Python is fetched.
uv can download and install the pinned CPython 3.11.15 build on the Windows executor without a checksum-verified Chocolatey package.
The current windows_release_wheel job hangs during the Chocolatey Python installation step on scheduled main runs.
With UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE set to only-managed, uv python find resolves to the uv-managed interpreter that uv build and the verification step both use.
The environment variable UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE is set to only-managed for the windows_release_wheel job.
The deep pip install and import check in the windows_release_wheel job passes once the interpreter comes from uv.
These harness helpers select only real serving workers as the kill victim, so they never kill the resource tracker process.
A kill call returns only after the supervisor has reaped the victim worker, and the replacement worker's readiness is awaited before the call returns.
Proxies launched with the lenient healthcheck use the graceful stop budget so killed workers respawn promptly.
OwnedProxy.suspended is only usable on a proxy launched with the lenient healthcheck.
Timing bounds are computed against either a configured product value or a measured control duration, not fixed literal numbers.
run.py measures proxy import time and derives the readiness budget (previously 70 s) and per-test budget (previously 90 s) from that measurement.

assumptions.target: OS connection distribution across proxy workers
assumptions.claim: Burst tests can steer roughly half the traffic to each worker by suspending the other worker, so they no longer depend on the OS spreading connections evenly.
The integration test tree has zero violations of TQ010 (raw signals) and TQ011 (literal elapsed caps) after the migration.
The /v1/decisions route exists on the proxy and routes through the same spend-tracking biller as /v1/systemone.
The /v1/systemone route exists on the proxy and writes SpendLogs rows through the shared biller.
ProxyClient does not yet have a decisions method, and this PR adds one for the new suite to call.
ProxyClient does not yet have a systemone method, and this PR adds one for the new suite to call.
Responses from both routes return a cost header that matches the cost recorded on the corresponding SpendLogs row.
The /model/info endpoint reports per-token input and output rates for every deployment under test, and those rates are the source of truth for expected spend.

OPENAI_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY with CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, DATABRICKS_API_KEY with DATABRICKS_API_BASE, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY are set in the e2e environment from the Shared vault.
OpenRouter has no cost-map row, and the cost it reports in the usage field is positive and is the value billed to spend.
OpenAI deployments accept a prompt_cache_breakpoint field with mode "explicit" on a content block, which places a cache breakpoint at that block.
OpenAI request payloads accept a prompt_cache_options field whose mode "implicit" enables caching when a breakpoint is present.
The chat completions entry point currently strips a client-sent cache_control for api.openai.com and forwards it raw to custom base URLs.
The messages entry point currently flattens a marked system block into the OpenAI instructions field, where no breakpoint can be placed.
Claude deployments currently receive cache_control exactly as the client sent it, and this change leaves that path unmodified.
A deployment uses the OpenAI dialect when its host is api.openai.com or when prompt_cache_options is set on it.
Cache marks on assistant turns, tool turns, and tool_result blocks cannot be represented in the OpenAI dialect and are therefore safe to drop.
The class attribute scans_attachments exists on CustomGuardrail with default False and is checked with an identity comparison (is True) by the four translation handlers.
Only BedrockGuardrail sets scans_attachments to True, and every other guardrail class leaves it at the False default.
The current Bedrock guardrail scans only text parts and skips image-only turns entirely, while pdf, file, document and video attachments reach the model unscanned.
ApplyGuardrail accepts image items for inline png and jpeg content but has no content type for documents, so other attachment types cannot be scanned and must be refused.

Refusing unsupported attachments with the guardrail's 400 is an acceptable fail-closed behaviour, and deployments that relied on pdf, file, document, video, audio, remote url or file_id parts passing through will accept receiving 400 responses.
The attachment refusal runs before role scoping, so an attachment anywhere in the conversation is refused even when experimental_use_latest_role_message_only is enabled.
Parts such as a bare {"type": "input_audio"} with no payload carry nothing to leak and can safely be dropped rather than refused.
Pull requests touching MCP gateway paths currently get no code owner review requests beyond the catch-all LiteLLM Engineering team.
The CODEOWNERS file on main was rewritten by #43653, and the branch's changes apply cleanly on top of that rewritten version.
The two cost map owner lines already present on main are correct and should be left unchanged.
GitHub automatically requests review from the owners listed in CODEOWNERS for files a pull request changes, based on last matching pattern.
These GitHub accounts exist and are valid members with write access to the BerriAI/litellm repository so they can be assigned as code owners.
Dashboard MCP, agents, and skills pages live under the paths named in the CODEOWNERS entries this PR adds, and those paths are not owned by the dashboard owners removed from main.
Before this change, each streamed tool_call delta from the Ollama chat transformation was emitted with index=0 regardless of which parallel tool call it belonged to.
The Ollama server returns multiple parallel tool calls in a single streaming response, each identified by its position in the response, so per-call index can be derived from that position.

assumptions.target: downstream clients accumulating tool_call arguments by index

assumptions.claim: SAP content blocks and tool schemas have a field that can carry cache_control markers without being rejected.
The captured request body at commit 53308754bb correctly reflects the cache_control markers that SAP receives.
The responses stream iterator currently yields the wrapper event to the logging path, so non-streaming callers do not get a completed response logged.

Affected providers always return SSE from the responses sub-call, even when the client did not request streaming.

The completed response object emitted at end of the SSE stream carries a usage block with token counts usable for spend calculation.
Existing tests cover the streaming path so that changing the non-streaming logging path does not regress streaming logging.
The sap/ provider currently flattens message content into plain strings and drops cache_control markers from messages and tools before sending requests.

assumptions.claim: Anthropic prompt caching does not activate through the SAP Orchestration /v2/completion endpoint today because cache_control is never forwarded to it.
The SAP Orchestration /v2/completion endpoint accepts content as a list of blocks and accepts cache_control fields on content blocks and tools.
Message content can be represented as a list of typed blocks, and a block can carry a cache_control object that LiteLLM preserves through the request path.
A local stand-in for the token endpoint, deployment discovery and /v2/completion faithfully mimics the real SAP Orchestration deployment, so the verified behaviour should transfer to a real tenant.
No real SAP AI Core credentials are available, so the change has not been verified against a live SAP tenant.

Unknown or ignored query arguments are rejected by strict validation rather than silently discarded.
Legacy pagination cursors are removed and will not be accepted by the query API.
The current trace listing endpoint returns unsorted rows and does not honour sort_by and sort_dir parameters.
The current raw SQL endpoint does not support native parameter binding through a params field.

The existing framer's block_end function already detects SSE event boundaries correctly and can be reused to split a complete buffered body.
Currently a cache hit replays the entire cached SSE body as a single chunk rather than one chunk per event.
The Python adapter already replays cached streams one event per chunk, which is the behaviour the Rust side should match.
The cached body is a complete, buffered SSE payload that can be split at event delimiters without needing live-stream handling.
SseCodec remains the correct tool for live streams and is unaffected by the new RawBlocks iterator.
Existing tests assert byte-identical output and ordering for cached SSE replay, so splitting into per-event chunks will keep them passing.
A new resolve_key method can be added to ResponseCacheService and called once per call by core, returning the key the cache will use.
The native default resolve_key returns cache_key(&request.key), so native cache keys are unchanged by this PR.
The Python cache object exposes get_cache_key(**kwargs), which can be called once per call over the new CacheCall::ResolveKey variant.
A caller-supplied cache_key kwarg takes precedence over get_cache_key, matching the precedence already used by Python's get_cache and add_cache.
Python cache lookup and store currently run under a key that differs from the one reported to callbacks and response metadata when a preset key or request namespace is used.
When key resolution fails, the system skips caching and calls the provider directly.
The Rust messages route currently reports a cache_key in response metadata and logging callbacks that does not match the key Python stored the entry under when a request namespace is set.
Event-framed replay and bounded stream capture are follow-up PRs that will be stacked on top of this change, so this PR does not include them.
Currently, with no cached or refreshable token, get_access_token starts the interactive device code login synchronously, which blocks the calling thread.
The device code login polls via httpx and time.sleep for up to 15 minutes before timing out.
chatgpt/* provider resolution during auth and budget checks runs on the proxy event loop, so a synchronous device flow there freezes the whole worker including health probes.
Calling asyncio.get_running_loop (or an equivalent check) from within get_access_token reliably detects whether an event loop is currently running on the calling thread.
A synchronous caller such as a terminal litellm.completion invocation has no running event loop and can still complete the interactive device code login.
Cached tokens and refresh-token renewal succeed inside a running event loop without triggering the device code flow.
The STREAM_CACHE_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES setting defaults to 4 MiB (4194304 bytes) and can be overridden by the STREAM_CACHE_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES environment variable.
ResponseCacheConfig exposes a max_entry_bytes field that core capture_stream reads to bound how much of a stream is captured.
Core capture_stream currently captures streams without any size limit before this change.
The legacy Anthropic Messages stream cache writer currently buffers the entire stream in memory with no size limit.
litellm-cache-response defines DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES and native v2 PyO3 defaults use the literal 4194304, which a compile-time assert pins to the same value.
The cached stream entry format is an event list whose shape is unchanged by this change.
The litellm-cache-response crate is a dependency available to the Python-backed Rust cache adapter that reads the limit.
The proxy returns a video id that is expected to encode the deployment's model_id when a per-model litellm_params.api_key is configured.
Status and content retrieval resolve the deployment and its per-model API key from the model_id embedded in the video id.
Passing model_id=None produces an encoded id whose decoded model_id is empty, which is the cause of the lost deployment key.
These provider transforms re-encode the returned video id with model_id=None, dropping the deployment's model_id.
No global OPENAI_API_KEY is configured in the affected deployment, so the provider-level fallback key is unavailable.
Existing tests cover encoding and decoding of video ids, and the new regression tests can exercise status and content retrieval with a per-model key.
The discovery component currently treats the workspace root and the user home directory as watched resources when a user-level instruction file exists.
The process-wide onDidFilesChange stream delivers changes for files anywhere under the home directory, not just within a session's worktree.
The affects() matcher returns true for any change at or inside the watched path, which is why changes under ~ refresh every loaded session.
The contains() matcher, with its change-type filter, can restrict matching to only the named file or only ADDED/DELETED events on a path.
Each call to discover on copilot-runtime is CPU-expensive enough that frequent invocations pin the CPU.
Customization locations are computed once per session and are not recomputed when files change during the session's lifetime.
The current logging dedup exempts streaming requests from deduplication, so streamed success events are not suppressed by the dedup flag.
Failure callbacks fire once per retry attempt for a request that is retried, producing one log entry per attempt.
The s3_v2 callback uploads one object per logged event keyed by request id, so duplicate failure events produce duplicate uploads.
Setting the dedup flag on a failure event is sufficient to suppress further failure logs for the same request id, including for streaming requests.
The deployment is configured with num_retries: 2, causing up to three attempts for a failing request.
The existing test suite covering the logging dedup behaviour is runnable locally with uv run pytest and passes after this change.
The connect, disconnect, failure, and cancellation telemetry events currently include connector names in their emitted payload.
The telemetry contract for connection-action events defines a connector name field that is currently present.
Existing tests assert payloads for connect, disconnect, failure, and cancellation events that include connector names.
The bridge currently calls destroy() on the browser-facing socket when the remote side closes, which discards any queued unwritten bytes.
The raw NodeSocket bridge already handles remote close by calling end(), so buffered bytes are flushed to the browser-facing socket.
Large responses forwarded from devcontainers in WSL are truncated because queued writes are dropped during socket teardown rather than flushed.

The Checked-JIT build asserts when GTF_EXCEPT flags are stale on nodes that no longer represent a throwing operation.
Normal (non-overflowing) shift counts continue to be recognized and folded into rotates after the new gtOverflow() guard is added.

assumptions.target: JIT morphing of SIMD partial stores
assumptions.claim: The current morphing of assignments to a SIMD field reads the full vector before evaluating the RHS and then overwrites the whole vector, so side effects of the RHS (such as a callee writing to other fields via ref) are lost.
The WithElement node is available in the JIT and can be used to represent a single-element replacement within a SIMD vector for side-effect-free RHS expressions.
The JIT can determine whether an RHS expression has persistent or ordering side effects (e.g. calls taking ref to the vector, volatile reads) so that the morphing choice can be made correctly.
Test infrastructure exists to add regression cases covering numerics-field and SIMD-half partial stores, plus assignment, pure-RHS and volatile-read scenarios.
The reported miscompilation in issue #135392 is caused by the full-vector read preceding the RHS evaluation in partial SIMD stores.
The current implementation discards the task returned by the chained sorter's key computation, so subsequent key selectors may not have completed before sorting reads their keys.
Exceptions thrown by secondary and later key selectors are currently swallowed and not propagated to the caller of the ordered sequence.
The sorter's ComputeKeysAsync method accepts elements, count and a cancellation token and returns an awaitable that completes once the chained keys are computed.
ThenBy and ThenByDescending chain a subsequent sorter via the _next field, which is null when no further ordering is specified.
The test suite does not currently include deterministic suspended-selector cases for secondary and third-level ordering, so these scenarios are not covered by existing tests.

Reading Delegate.Method on an open delegate to a private generic-base method currently resolves the method against the delegate's derived first-argument type rather than the exact generic base instantiation.

Reading Delegate.Method in this scenario currently triggers an assertion in Checked CoreCLR builds.
The existing test suite has no coverage for this scenario, so the new regression tests are the first to exercise it.
The runtime can resolve a method against its exact generic base instantiation from an open delegate's first-argument type without additional type-system support.

Restores of the affected projects fail with NU1904 before the update and succeed after it with both packages resolving to 2.5.11.
The lowering phase can currently move a cneg instruction ahead of its cmp instruction during store-pair formation, which breaks flags dependencies.

The reported UnsafeAccessor scenario depends on a module initializer that writes a private field, which is skipped under the current inlining behaviour.
The global module type's TypeDef token is stable across versions of the referenced assembly, so it can be referenced outside the version bubble.
Ordinary TypeDef tokens outside the version bubble are not stable and must still be rejected by the existing checks.
Test infrastructure can generate assembly references that a test reader decodes to verify activation fixups.
Composite ReadyToRun images are produced by the toolchain in a form where cross-module inlining within the composite image occurs as described.
The IsAuthenticated property exists on NegotiateAuthentication and reports whether the authentication exchange has completed.
GetOutgoingBlob returns a status code that callers can inspect to determine the outcome of each authentication step.
The TargetName property's XML documentation currently references IsAuthenticated in a way that is misleading and needs removal.
IsAuthenticated can be true when the exchange has completed without the authentication having succeeded, so it does not by itself indicate success.
The XML comments in the NegotiateAuthentication source file are the content that surfaces in IntelliSense for consumers.
The referenced upstream documentation changes in dotnet/dotnet-api-docs#12724 are correct and can be ported as-is.
The EventPipe writer path in NativeAOT currently proceeds without waiting for in-flight writers, so a use-after-free is possible when a session is torn down concurrently with an active writer.
CoreCLR waits for active writers to finish before releasing shared EventPipe state, and the new NativeAOT logic mirrors that behaviour.
The release/10.0 branch already contains the code from #134838 that is being backported, or the change applies cleanly on top of it.
The existing test suite passes with the change, and no dedicated regression test exists because the crash is intermittent and was validated via code review only.
The reported intermittent crashes with clrmd and EventSourceSupport stem from the EventPipe use-after-free addressed by this change.
Passive lookups currently read g_pSyncTable without first acquiring the object-header bits, so an older table base can be combined with a newer index.
The object-header bits can be read with acquire ordering and used to validate and decode the SyncBlock index before the indexed table entry is read.
A newly allocated SyncBlock index is currently published without a release barrier guaranteeing the SyncBlock is fully initialized first.
The precious and disposable SyncBlock state is obsolete and no remaining code path depends on it.
The GC cleanup helpers being removed are unused anywhere else in the runtime.
Existing tests cover concurrent sync-table lookups and SyncBlock publication sufficiently to catch regressions from the ordering change.
The Linux inotify event-processing loop in FileSystemWatcher currently returns false on an unpaired IN_MOVED_FROM event, which silently stops the watcher.
The FileSystemWatcher rewrite in .NET 11 means the affected Linux code path no longer exists there, so the bug is not reproducible on .NET 11.
The regression was introduced by change #9130, which shipped in .NET 9 and is present in the release/10.0 servicing branch.
The customer-provided repro app reproduces the silent watcher stop after a merge that moves directories on both sides, and the fix resolves it.

Replacing return false with break in the foreach loop only changes the narrow error/cleanup path for an unmatched IN_MOVED_FROM on a previously-watched subdirectory, leaving watch removal, event dispatch and loop state reset unchanged.
No automated regression test is needed because a test for this scenario would be flaky and the code path is unlikely to regress in the servicing branch.
The sync index is published to other threads by a write that can become visible before the corresponding SyncTable growth is visible on weakly ordered hardware such as ARM64.
Table accesses following the header read are not ordered after that read without an acquire load, so an undersized table can be observed alongside a newly published index.
Header loads currently use plain (non-acquire) reads on the SyncTable lookup path.
Issue 135173 describes a memory-ordering bug where a new sync index can pair with an older, undersized SyncTable on ARM64.
NativeAOT currently returns null for Type.Namespace on nested generic types even though their FullName is namespace-qualified.
The metadata writer currently emits namespace definitions for nested types, which the schema does not require and which this change must stop.
Namespace resolution for a nested type can be performed by walking up to its enclosing types and reading their namespace.
Well-known attribute matching currently applies to nested types as well as top-level types, so nested attribute lookalikes can be mistaken for the real attributes.
The existing test suite has no coverage for nested generic definitions, nested generic constructions, global-namespace nesting, or nested attribute lookalikes, so new cases are needed.
Issue 135106 describes the null Type.Namespace behaviour on nested generic types that this PR addresses.
Plain (non-acquire) reads of the type-loading flags can observe completed type loading before the payload writes that precede it are visible, so readers need acquire semantics on the flags.
Writers of the type-loading completion flags use interlocked operations that publish the payload before setting the flag, so an acquire read of the flag suffices to make prior payload writes visible.
A child type can currently observe null inherited dictionary pointers when it reads readiness state with plain loads on Arm64.
VolatileLoad provides acquire load semantics suitable for reading the MethodTable type-loading flags.
These MethodTable readiness queries each read the type-loading flags and can be routed through a single centralized acquire snapshot without changing their results.
Both TypeDesc readiness queries can each be served by exactly one acquire read of the flags per call.
Existing loader locking discipline and the numeric values and layouts of the type-loading flags remain unchanged by this change.
Concurrent first loads can currently publish an All coverage marker for a constraint array that is only partially populated.
A compare-and-swap publish of a zero-initialized candidate array is available and atomically establishes a single shared array across concurrent builders.

assumptions.target: losing builders in the constraint cache
assumptions.claim: A builder whose compare-and-swap fails can adopt the already-published array and discard its own candidate without side effects.
The coverage compare-and-swap is performed only after all slot stores it promises have completed, so readers observing All coverage see fully filled slots.
Generic types with zero constraints already behave correctly and the change leaves their handling unchanged.
Existing tests exercise concurrent first loads of constraint caches so regressions in publication ordering would be caught.
The JIT currently removes empty try/finally regions and mishandles handler-entry reference counting, causing an assertion failure in the reported case.
The reported assertion failure during removal of an empty try-catch-fault reproduces on the current codebase and is the issue this PR addresses.
A focused regression test for the empty try/catch/fault removal scenario can be added and run as part of the existing CoreCLR test conventions.
A CoreCLR baseline build succeeds before any code changes are applied, so the subsequent fix can be validated against it.
CI build context and CodeQL analysis are available to validate the change before it is finalized.
Reflection invocation can return a byref pointing into a helper's temporary argument storage, which becomes invalid once the helper returns.
The five invocation helpers currently return a byref result rather than an object, so dereferencing happens after argument storage and GC registrations may have expired.
MethodInfo.Invoke on NativeAOT can surface a ref-return whose dereferenced value is stale or incorrect when read after the helper returns.

assumptions.target: MethodInvoker span and fixed-argument invocation paths
assumptions.claim: MethodInvoker span and fixed-argument invoke paths share the same ref-return lifetime issue as MethodInfo.Invoke.
The existing reflection smoke test exists and can be extended with one-, four-, and five-argument ref-return cases.

assumptions.target: copy-back and exception wrapping in invocation helpers
assumptions.claim: Copy-back of by-ref arguments and exception wrapping behave correctly and need not change to fix the lifetime problem.
The MsQuic version bundled by this release branch is the updated version that changed the error code returned for ephemeral-key certificates.
MsQuic now surfaces SEC_E_UNKNOWN_CREDENTIALS when an application uses a certificate with an ephemeral key on Windows.
Schannel, the Windows TLS provider, does not work with certificates whose private keys are ephemeral and not persisted in a key store.
Without this change, the .NET application receives a hard-to-diagnose exception rather than a helpful diagnostic exception for ephemeral-key certificates.
The test failures addressed by this PR are caused by the changed MsQuic error code and are the only failures this change needs to fix.
The fix can be applied to release/8.0 without conflicting with the MsQuic update already present on that branch.
The managed ilasm tool currently accepts the /FOLD command-line option.

assumptions.claim: Managed ilasm emits method bodies exactly as it does today when /FOLD is not specified.
A complete method body, including its header and exception regions, can be serialized to bytes so that byte-identical bodies can be detected.
Existing tests cover the current behaviour of ilasm emission and option handling that this change must preserve.
The NativeAOT EventPipe currently lets threads write to event buffers without waiting for in-flight writers, so a use-after-free can occur when a session is torn down.
CoreCLR EventPipe waits for active writers to finish before releasing shared resources, and the new NativeAOT logic matches that behaviour.
Customers using clrmd with EventSourceSupport can hit the intermittent crash addressed by this change.
No deterministic test reproduces the crash, so correctness rests on code review rather than an automated test.
The change applies cleanly to release/11.0 as a backport of #134838 from the main branch.
The flush sentinel table is length 3 with element 0 holding auxiliary data and two entries, so a length-2 check never matches it.
Every flush re-installs the same shared sentinel table instance rather than allocating a fresh one.
Entries inserted while the sentinel is installed are written into the shared sentinel table and persist across subsequent flushes.
Stale cached targets from unloaded collectible AssemblyLoadContexts can be returned once their native addresses are reused.
CacheElementCount(table) returns the number of usable entries, excluding the auxiliary element 0, and can be used to identify the sentinel.
The regression test reproduces the stale-entry failure against unfixed CoreLib and passes with the fix.
Other existing tests in the Loader/CollectibleAssemblies suite pass with this change.
The baseline build with ./build.sh clr+libs -lc release -rc checked succeeds on this branch.
The NativeAOT compiler already defines a TentativeMethodNode type that this change can implement for the WASM backend.
The WASM backend currently cannot emit tentative method stubs, so no stub-emission path exists yet for WASM.
The WASM object writer exposes a registration mechanism for tentative method signatures that can be called from the compiler.
The WASM object writer already supports function-index relocations that the NativeAOT emitter can use.
The target WASM runtime supports the tail-call proposal, so return_call is a valid instruction to emit for forwarding to the real method body.
The managed calling convention parameters can be forwarded unchanged to the selected target from a stub with the same signature.
The managed HttpListener parser currently accepts whitespace after a chunk-size value rather than rejecting it as invalid chunk-size syntax.
The parser treats a semicolon as the start of an optional chunk extension, and everything before it is expected to be hexadecimal digits.
Valid hexadecimal chunk sizes are parsed correctly by the existing code and will remain unaffected by the stricter validation.
The existing HttpListener test suite runs and passes, providing a baseline against which the new raw chunked-request test is added.
A test harness exists that can send raw HTTP bytes including chunked bodies to an HttpListener and observe whether the request is rejected.
Issue #132746 describes the problem of whitespace being accepted in chunk-size fields and is the reference for this change.

assumptions.target: HttpListener rejection of malformed chunked requests
assumptions.claim: Rejecting a malformed chunked request is the expected server response, and the listener surfaces it as a protocol error rather than silently truncating the body.
Package authoring steps in the csproj are not needed for this change in .NET 9, so no project version or package metadata edits are required.
MakeGeneric performs a constraint check against interface constraints of generic type parameters at runtime.
Without the TypeMetadataNode change, an interface constraint can end up being an unresolvable TypeRef in the generated output.
InterfaceUse is not propagated across the scanning/compilation boundary, so tracking interface uses with it only works in modes without the scanner.
Reflected types are propagated across the scanning/compilation boundary and can serve as the basis for tracking interface uses.
GenericTypeDefinitionNode does not currently report interface use, but other EEType nodes already do.
Treating a reflected interface type as used is a sufficient overapproximation to keep interface constraints validatable in MakeGeneric.
Runtime size measurements show that the added interface use reporting and metadata changes have no meaningful size impact.
Dynamic method collection can currently encounter unpublished code headers that the unwind info table does not expect, causing the access violation.
Discarded allocations during dynamic method creation are cleaned up in a way that the baseline build can confirm and reproduce.
No focused tests currently cover DynamicMethod collection, so new coverage must be added to exercise the unpublished code header path.
A complete baseline build of the repository can be produced in the current environment to establish pre-change behaviour.
Validation is limited to certain platforms, and results on other platforms cannot be confirmed by this change.
Currently the covariant array store check is skipped when the element type is exact and the value handle equals the element handle, which is unsound for shared generic instantiations like G<__Canon>.

assumptions.target: crossgen2 and ILC array parameter typing
assumptions.claim: Crossgen2 and NativeAOT report the precise G<__Canon>[] type for shared-code parameters, while plain JIT reports __Canon[], which is not sealed.
The helper eeIsSharedInst exists in the JIT and returns true for handles representing shared (canonical) instantiations, and is already used by VN's exact-type IND(obj) folding.
The compareTypesForCast == Must path and the exact object[] path already return conservative answers for shared types, so they do not need changes.
Store checks for arrays of unshared sealed element types can still be safely skipped by the existing handle-equality shortcut.
The JIT already contains a guard that rejects shared-instance types before folding Enum.HasFlag to a payload comparison, and this PR can mirror that guard for Enum.Equals.
The JIT currently folds Enum.Equals to a payload comparison whenever canonical handles match, without first rejecting shared-instance types.
Nested enums under shared generic instantiations such as C<string>.E and C<object>.E share a canonical handle while having distinct runtime types.
A test harness exists that can be parameterized over equal and unequal payloads across shared and non-shared enum types so new regression cases can be added.
The JIT's type canonicalization for shared generics is the mechanism that causes distinct instantiations to produce matching canonical handles.
GenTreeCall exposes a NeedsNullCheck() predicate that reports whether the call carries GTF_CALL_NULLCHECK.
The JIT currently converts tail-recursive calls to loops without checking whether the call requires a receiver null check, so the null check is dropped.
When loop conversion is skipped, the fast-tail-call path still emits the receiver null check for non-virtual callvirt calls.
Disabling caller optimization prevents inlining of the recursive method's callees, so the tail call remains visible to the optimizer for the test.

assumptions.target: JIT regression test for tail-recursion receiver null checks
assumptions.claim: The added regression test runs with null and non-null receivers at zero, one, and multiple recursion depths and is able to observe a NullReferenceException when the bug is present.
Non-virtual callvirt calls carry GTF_CALL_NULLCHECK so the JIT must emit an explicit receiver null check for them.
Explicit and sequential derived reference types can start their field layout from the parent's laid-out instance size when the base already has explicit or sequential layout.
The runtime treats an explicit or sequential base layout as an already-materialized prefix, so the aligned field-base-offset path must not be reused for these inheritance shapes.
The temporary TypeLoadException workaround blocking precompilation for these inheritance shapes is no longer needed once Crossgen2 computes the layout itself.
The ReadyToRun block for Github13362 was a workaround that hid a real layout mismatch between compile-time and runtime field offsets.
Field verification currently fails for a sequential base with an explicit derived type (and the inverse) because compile-time and runtime field offsets disagree.
GenBase<T> is a sequential-layout class with two string fields, and GenInt is an explicit-layout derived class placing its string fields at offsets 0 and 16 relative to the object.
ProcessStartInfo exposes a PseudoTerminal property that, when set, causes the started process to be attached to a pseudo-terminal instead of plain pipes.

ThrowIfInvalid currently rejects StandardInputEncoding and StandardOutputEncoding whenever redirection is combined with a PTY, and this PR relaxes that check so those encodings are allowed when PTY is used.
With PTY enabled, the process's stderr is not exposed as a separate stream and is instead observed through StandardOutput.
On Unix, when no StandardInputEncoding or StandardOutputEncoding is specified for a PTY-backed process, the PTY streams default to UTF-8 without a byte order mark.
The Unix platform provides native pseudo-terminal allocation functions that the native shim can call during process startup.
PTY tests run only on platforms and environments where pseudo-terminal support is available and are skipped otherwise.
Existing PTY tests pass on the target platforms and the new encoding and default-encoding tests exercise the updated behaviour.
The Requires.ValidateRange helper exists and performs the same range validation as the two-line overflow-safe check it replaces.
The two conflicting versions of the range validation in ImmutableArray_1.cs both enforce identical bounds semantics, so keeping one version preserves behaviour.
The two-line overflow-safe check on main is correct and fully covered by the Requires.ValidateRange call that is being kept.
Existing tests cover the range validation paths in ImmutableArray_1.cs so the merge resolution is verified.
The test-only Utf8BomInsertingStream class does not currently override ReadAsync, so async reads fall through to the base Stream implementation.
The base Stream.ReadAsync routes through BeginEndReadAsync and BeginReadInternal(serializeAsynchronously: true), scheduling the synchronous Read on a ThreadPool thread via Task.Factory.StartNew.
The wrapped underlying stream is a MemoryStream with no real I/O, so synchronous reads complete immediately and offloading them to the ThreadPool is unnecessary.
The test is expected to throw NotSupportedException, and the intermittent NullReferenceException arises only from the async deserialization error path reached via the ThreadPool hop.
The Memory<byte> overload exists on the target framework under #if NET, so an override with that signature compiles there.
MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray is available on the targeted runtimes and can be used as a fast path for the Memory<byte> overload.
The ILLink trimmer tests pass on the current branch state.
The Roslyn analyzer tests pass on the current branch state.
DataFlowTests.cs already contains the test-entry registration pattern used by sibling data flow test files, so a new entry can be added to it.
The trimmer reports DAM-related warnings on delegate invocation using the message text referring to 'Invoke' rather than the field or property name.
DynamicallyAccessedMembers annotations on generic type parameters do not propagate to a delegate's Invoke method, so the GenericDelegateWithAnnotatedTypeParameter class is dead code.
The test file DelegateDataFlow.cs compiles as a standalone test case under the shared test infrastructure.
The NativeAOT test run uses the same shared test infrastructure and the aotsdk build artifacts it requires are available in the environment.
The generated marshaller exposes a GetManagedValuesSource method that returns a span or collection whose Length equals the number of managed elements to clean up.
The managed collection is the authoritative source of element count during ManagedToUnmanaged cleanup, so its length matches the number of unmanaged elements allocated during marshalling.

assumptions.claim: Prior to this change the generator emitted a hardcoded numElements = 0 in cleanup, causing element Free calls to be skipped and unmanaged memory to leak.
StatelessMarshallingStrategy.cs can call the base-class method GenerateNumElementsAssignmentFromManagedValuesSource() once it is exposed on the base class in ElementsMarshalling.cs.
