assumptions.claim: The outer cleanup scope already declares the unmanaged span, and inner element cleanup can reference the outer managed span by indexing it as managedSpan[index].
Existing generator snapshot and runtime tests cover jagged array marshalling with element marshallers that define Free, and will validate the new cleanup output.
The SDK already sets MetadataUpdaterSupport to false for non-Debug builds, so ILLink.targets does not need to set it at all.
Currently StartupHookSupport is unconditionally defaulted to false for trimmed/AOT builds regardless of configuration, which blocks Hot Reload in Debug builds.
The Configuration property is defined with a value of 'Debug' when a Debug build is requested, so the condition can distinguish Debug from non-Debug builds.
Preserving startup hooks in Debug AOT builds is sufficient to enable Hot Reload in those apps.
Correctness of this change is verified in the SDK repository rather than by tests included in this PR.
System.ValueTuple is pulled into the NuGet dependency graph of net471 projects through the net462 dependency group of the affected packages.
net471 includes System.ValueTuple as an inbox assembly, so it does not need to be supplied by a NuGet package.
NuGet selects the net462 dependency group for net471 consumers when no net471 group exists, causing System.ValueTuple to be resolved.
Thirteen packages directly reference System.ValueTuple through their net462 dependency groups and are the ones receiving a net471 group.
Adding a net471 dependency group without additional assemblies is sufficient to prevent System.ValueTuple from entering the net471 graph.
The net462 assemblies of the affected packages are source identical to what net471 would need, so no net471 assemblies need to be shipped.
The DependencyOnlyTargetFrameworks mechanism is supported by the build tooling to emit a dependency group without shipping assemblies for that target framework.
The attribute currently only has a constructor taking a Type, so a parameterless constructor overload is added by this change and does not already exist.
The attribute's AttributeUsage currently excludes Struct, so extending targets to include Struct is needed for struct support.
Currently every serializable type must be listed via a separate JsonSerializerContext-derived class annotated with JsonSerializable(typeof(T)) to get generated JsonTypeInfo.
The existing source generator has a single incremental pipeline keyed on JsonSerializerContext-derived classes that can be extended with a second pipeline in Roslyn4.0 and Roslyn3.11 variants.
The generator must support both Roslyn 3.11 and Roslyn 4.0 APIs, with equivalent logic in each variant.
A CP0015 suppression for the AttributeUsageAttribute change on JsonSerializableAttribute is an acceptable baseline entry for this breaking-looking change.
A partial POCO annotated with parameterless JsonSerializable can have a generated static JsonTypeInfo property added without conflicting with user-declared members.
Existing source generator tests continue to pass unchanged after the new pipeline is added, so the reflection-free path for type-annotated contexts is unaffected.
The supplemental API documentation articles linked from the new remarks will be available once dotnet/docs#51571 has merged.

The existing libraries tests are expected to pass unchanged in behaviour after the migration from xunit v2 to xunit v3, with production code untouched.
The ComputeIlcCompileInputs target runs after ResolvedFileToPublish has been populated in the publish pipeline when RunILLink is true.

The ILLink step runs before ComputeIlcCompileInputs and its output is what gets registered in ResolvedFileToPublish.
fgMorphArgs can be called directly on a freshly created GenTreeCall node after rationalization and performs only ABI info and argument processing.
fgMorphTree routes through fgMorphCall, which performs tail-call analysis, inline marking, and GC safe-point flagging that are unnecessary at these post-rationalization call sites.

Existing fgMorphArgs call sites in Lower were previously guarded by a hack comment about safely calling fgMorphTree, and their intent is now correctly described by the new comments.

The GS cookie check call created after rationalization needs only argument/ABI processing and no further morph-time call analysis.

The ILTrim expected-failure entries for the debugger-related cases correspond to tests that now pass with this change.

The compiler in use recognizes the updated-memory-safety-rules feature flag, so adding it unconditionally does not cause a build error.

XmlRawWriter exposes a char[]-based WriteRaw method that serves as the existing string-based fallback for raw text output.

Indent writer variants set mixed-content state correctly when raw text is written through their existing write paths.
The existing test suite includes coverage for primitive array serialization that the new Xml_DecimalArrayAsRoot test can extend.

ServiceProvider can be extended to implement IServiceKeysProvider without conflicting with its existing public surface.

assumptions.target: project and resource files in the repository
assumptions.claim: Files matching csproj, locproj, nativeproj, proj, resx, slnx and vbproj extensions are expected to be UTF-8 without BOM.
Pre-existing files outside the PR's changed set may violate the charset rule without causing the build to fail.
Block currently disables thread priority boost on Windows via SetThreadPriorityBoost around the _blocker.TimedWait call, and this is the existing wake-preemption suppression the change mirrors.
The new native function sets the calling thread to SCHED_BATCH and is a no-op on non-Linux Unix targets.
The new native function restores the calling thread to SCHED_OTHER with priority 0 without capturing or restoring any prior scheduler state.
Threadpool threads run at default scheduler settings (SCHED_OTHER, priority 0), so resetting to defaults after the wait is correct and discarding prior user-set scheduler state is acceptable.
Wake-preemption suppression is scoped exactly to the _blocker.TimedWait window inside LowLevelLifoSemaphore.Block.
The Linux kernel supports the SCHED_BATCH policy for per-thread scheduling on the calling thread without requiring elevated privileges.
Calls using the async calling convention are currently imported by impSetupAsyncCall without rejection, so a non-async caller can contain such a call and reach the JIT.
A non-task-returning async method invoked from a non-async caller is never transformed by the async phase and leads to undefined behavior at runtime.
The AsyncHelpers.AsyncCallContinuation intrinsic exists and is imported after the async call in the task-returning thunk and resumption stub, so the check must be deferred to post-import.
The compUsesAsyncContinuation flag is set whenever a method uses the AsyncCallContinuation intrinsic and is reliable as the signal distinguishing legal non-async callers.

The existing native deflate state supports a reset operation that returns it to a reusable clean state for a new compression run.

clamped_poisson_interval has several callers, and only core_policy.py currently guards base_delay > 0 before calling it.
A zero or negative average interval unambiguously means no wait, so returning 0.0 is the correct result for non-positive intervals.
The existing test suite for the math helper does not yet cover non-positive average intervals, so new tests can be added there for inputs 0, 0.0 and -1.
docker-py's container.wait() forwards its timeout argument to the underlying requests call, so passing None leaves the wait unbounded.
The DOCKER_CLIENT_TIMEOUT setting does not apply to container.wait() when no timeout argument is passed, so the wait request currently can block indefinitely.

When an exception is raised after the flow run has been reported as started, BaseWorker logs a 'Lost connection to flow run infrastructure' message, releases the concurrency slot, and does not mark the run as Crashed.
Expiry of the wait timeout raises requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout and does not stop the container, which continues running and reports its own final state.
The configuration model accepts an optional positive integer field, so validation rejects zero or negative values for container_wait_timeout.
Existing and new tests exercise the wait call with a mocked Docker client, so no real Docker daemon is required to verify the timeout is forwarded.

Before this change, the sync task engine always passes write_result=True when persisting a failed task's exception, regardless of persist_result.
Before this change, the async task engine omits the write_result argument when calling exception_to_failed_state, so it defaults to False and the exception is never written to result storage.

A Failed state with ResultRecordMetadata attached points to a result file that must actually exist in storage, otherwise aresult() raises ValueError 'Path ... does not exist.'
should_persist_result() returns True exactly when the task's persist_result setting is enabled, and it is callable from both the sync and async task engine handle_exception paths.
get_result_store() returns a usable result store that writes results to storage when write_result is True.
The test module already exists and can host parametrized sync/async tests for failed task exception persistence.

The enforcer thread injects CancelledError into the supervised thread via PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc once the timeout elapses, with no check for whether the supervised thread has already exited the scope.
Scope exit joins the enforcer thread, so the supervised thread can block in __exit__ while the enforcer is still active.
The class does not currently have an _exit_lock or _exited attribute, so both must be introduced by this change.
Cancel callbacks run from the enforcer as soon as the timeout elapses and do not depend on exception delivery.
This test is the one that leaves the worker thread unfinished when the race occurs and is reproducible under CPU contention.
This test is the one reported as crashing the xdist worker after the stray exception is delivered, and it is not itself the source of the bug.
Setting this to DEBUG increases logging work inside the window where the async exception can land, making the race more likely to reproduce.
find_placeholders currently raises ValueError for None values instead of treating them as containing no placeholders.
find_placeholders returns early for int, float and bool values, so None can follow the same no-placeholder path.
apply_values already preserves None values, so JSON null survives placeholder substitution unchanged.
CustomWebhookNotificationBlock validates json_data by calling find_placeholders on its contents, so fixing find_placeholders also fixes webhook payload validation.
Other unsupported types such as tuples still raise ValueError and should continue to do so.
Rejection of unknown placeholders in json_data still works after the change.
Prior to this change, direct Docker submissions transport only the bundle JSON and drop files named in include_files.
Each submission can be staged in its own directory without colliding with other concurrent submissions that use identical included files.
The Docker runtime can mount the included-files archive beside the bundle into the container at execution time.
Configured storage accepts uploads of the content-addressed sidecar key and reports upload failures that can be detected and handled.
The existing ZIP extractor can unpack included files before execution and preserve executable permissions.
Work-pool submission with configured storage continues to use the existing generic upload path and is not affected by this change.

Prefect delivers task timeouts and cancellation as a CancelledError that is a BaseException, so it can be caught with a bare except BaseException clause.
dbtRunner.invoke runs on the calling thread and only tears down its worker pool and cancels open connections for KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and FailFastError, not for other BaseExceptions.
Current dbt behaviour swallows an unrecognised BaseException into dbtRunnerResult.exception rather than propagating it, while worker threads and in-flight queries keep running.
PrefectDbtRunner currently wraps a failed dbtRunnerResult in a ValueError, and a retry then starts a second dbt run while the first is still executing.
Injecting a KeyboardInterrupt into the dbt invocation thread triggers dbt's own shutdown path that tears down worker threads.
The dbt adapter exposes cancel_open_connections, which can be called under connection_named("master") to cancel in-flight queries.
dbtRunner.invoke can be run on a dedicated daemon thread with the caller's contextvars copied over and still produce the same result.
DbtCoreExecutor routes its dbt invocations through the same dbtRunner.invoke path as PrefectDbtRunner.
@biomejs/biome is a locked devDependency in ui-v2/package-lock.json at version 2.5.12.
The preceding npm ci step (or node_modules cache restore) installs @biomejs/biome into ui-v2/node_modules so that npx biome resolves to it.
Running npx biome ci from ui-v2 succeeds and checks 1523 files with the installed locked Biome binary.
The setup-biome action is the only source of the Biome binary in the lint job, so removing it leaves no other download step needed.
The Lint job failed on main because setup-biome received repeated HTTP 504 responses from the GitHub API and gave up after three retries.
A flow run acquires its deployment concurrency slot on the Scheduled to Pending transition when a worker submits it, up to PREFECT_WORKER_PREFETCH_SECONDS before its scheduled start.
A flow run keeps its deployment concurrency slot until it leaves Pending, Running, or Cancelling, with an in-process retry being the only exception.
With CANCEL_NEW and a concurrency limit of 1, a new scheduled run is cancelled with 'Deployment concurrency limit reached' when another run still holds the slot.
The worker prefetch window setting exists and determines how far before its scheduled start a run is submitted and takes its slot.
A run that is submitted but not yet Running keeps its deployment slot only if it reaches Running within grace_period_seconds.
flow.serve() accepts a prefetch_seconds argument on its runner that controls prefetch in place of the worker setting PREFECT_WORKER_PREFETCH_SECONDS.
The concepts page's Concurrency limiting section previously listed concurrency fields and collision strategies without describing when slots are acquired or released.
Prefect already provides a FileLock utility that can serialize filesystem index updates across server processes.
Stale expiration-index entries can exist for leases that have since been renewed or recreated, causing live leases to be wrongly revoked.
Expiration scans read index candidates without verifying them against the authoritative lease file before reporting them.
The memory backend does not currently update its stored expiration on lease renewal, so a pre-repossession expiration recheck would not work there.
Docket supports per-task keys that can be used to suppress duplicate scheduling of revocation tasks.
The existing stale-expiry-scan regression test exists and reproduces the stale index revocation bug before this change.
Two processes creating a lease concurrently can currently produce two lease files but only one index entry.
Filesystem locking does not combine lease storage with SQL accounting, so the formal model remains valid under this change.
The test passes on Python 3.12 without the skipif marker, so the skip is no longer needed.

The flow_run table has a state_type column that holds the flow run's state type and is filterable with IN lists.
The flow_run table has nullable start_time and expected_start_time columns whose coalesce defines the sort key used by START_TIME_ASC queries.

The flow runs filter endpoint compiles a state.type filter, a start_time bound, and sort=START_TIME_ASC into a WHERE state_type IN (...) AND coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time) <= cutoff query with ORDER BY on the same coalesce expression.
Existing expression indexes on coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time) in ascending and descending order exist and do not include state_type.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, pg_index.indisvalid, and REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY are available and behave as documented in the target PostgreSQL version.
The existing migration c8d5f2a71b3e implements an indisvalid check followed by REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY repair that can be reused as a pattern.
Offline SQL generation for the PostgreSQL migration is rejected because the migration must inspect the live catalog.

On SQLite, _notify registers an after_commit listener that calls run_coro_as_sync(automation_changed(...)) on the event-loop thread during session.commit().

The math writer creates a new tick on each run, so a conversation accumulates multiple ticks in the Delphi result families until a full Delphi run clears them.

The latest_math_tick field is always populated and identifies the newest tick for each conversation.
Archived older-tick rows are written to archived-<family>.jsonl files and are preserved there without being imported.

rat and rdt are already computed upstream as two-proportion z-scores that encode whether the group's agree or disagree rate is significantly higher than other groups' rates.

The Postgres english text-search parser tokenizes a hyphen directly before a digit run as a minus sign, so the digits are indexed with the hyphen included as a lexeme such as '-12345'.
Postgres prefix matching with the N:* form only matches lexemes that start with N, so it cannot match a lexeme like '-12345' and there is no suffix wildcard.
SqlPostStore.search swallows tsquery syntax errors and returns zero results when a parenthesised group appears inside a quoted tsquery operand.
The existing search index already contains lexemes such as '-12345' for posts with hyphenated numbers, so no migration or index rebuild is needed for the rewrite to find them.
Unquoted all-digit search terms, including N:* wildcard forms, reach the rewrite step as separate tokens before the tsquery is assembled, and quoted phrases are passed through untouched.
Excluded search terms go through the same tsquery assembly path, so applying the rewrite to them is sufficient to exclude both N and -N.

updatePost sets Posts.UpdateAt from model.GetMillis(), so its resolution is 1 millisecond and two writes within the same millisecond produce equal UpdateAt values.
BatchDelete calls updatePost to bump the post's UpdateAt, so the post's UpdateAt changes after a successful BatchDelete.
model.GetMillis returns the current wall-clock time in milliseconds and advances monotonically enough that a subsequent call returns a strictly larger value once a millisecond has elapsed.
The subtest is the only failing case and reproduces the flake because oldUpdateAt is captured immediately after SaveWithModel with no delay before BatchDelete runs.
require.Greater compares the two UpdateAt int64 values and fails when the updated value is not strictly greater than the old one.
The Postgres test database used by the storetest suite is available and runs the UPDATE statements synchronously within the test's goroutine.
Saving a reaction stamps Posts.UpdateAt using model.GetMillis(), which has only 1ms resolution.

The change introduced in #57292 is what allows redistributed commands to be rejected on the target partition with matching records.
Calling onlyCommands() on the RecordingExporter.records() stream restricts results to command records only, excluding events and rejections.

The gateway already exposes configurable server-side maxConnectionAge and maxConnectionAgeGrace settings, added in PR #60886, which currently default to null (disabled).
grpc-java's maxConnectionAgeGrace is the drain window after GOAWAY during which in-flight RPCs may complete before the connection is forcibly closed, and it does not extend the connection's lifetime.
Normal in-flight gateway RPCs complete well within 1 minute, so a 1m grace period is sufficient to avoid cutting off calls.
gRPC clients handle GOAWAY-driven connection closure by reconnecting gracefully, so periodic connection recycling every ~5-6 minutes does not cause client-visible failures.
No deployment or environment overrides the default maxConnectionAge or maxConnectionAgeGrace values, so changing the defaults to 5m and 1m takes effect in the benchmark environments.
The script is idempotent across reruns, so retrying the whole step after a partial run is safe because --skip-assigned skips issues already updated in a prior attempt.
The script runs under set -euo pipefail with no existing retry logic around its gh calls, so a single failing gh invocation aborts the entire job.
The script supports --direct, --updated-since 2h and --skip-assigned flags as used by the hourly cron invocation.
The cron job that keeps the Urgency field in sync runs the assign-urgency-to-issues.sh script hourly.
The gh CLI surfaces GitHub API transient failures such as HTTP 503 as a non-zero exit code that the cron step can detect and retry.
The HTTP 503 'No server is currently available' error observed in a recent run is transient and typically succeeds on resubmission.
grpc-java's NettyServerBuilder exposes maxConnectionAge(long, TimeUnit) that makes the server send GOAWAY after the configured connection age.
grpc-java's NettyServerBuilder exposes maxConnectionAgeGrace(long, TimeUnit) that bounds how long in-flight RPCs may continue after GOAWAY is sent.
When a server closes a connection with GOAWAY, grpc-java clients move the subchannel from READY to IDLE and trigger Helper#refreshNameResolution() so DNS is re-resolved.

Currently the gateway configures only maxInboundMessageSize and permitKeepAliveTime on its gRPC server, leaving maxConnectionAge and maxConnectionAgeGrace at grpc-java defaults (disabled, Long.MAX_VALUE).
The grpc-java version in use provides NettyServerBuilder.maxConnectionAge and maxConnectionAgeGrace with the described GOAWAY semantics.
The client-side decorator from the closed PR is no longer needed because server-side connection age achieves equivalent DNS re-resolution for all gRPC clients.
NetworkCfg can be extended with maxConnectionAge and maxConnectionAgeGrace settings that flow through to the gRPC server builder.
The handler currently returns AnalyticsCategory.CONTRACTUAL, so camunda.user_task.created is exported regardless of whether the optional category is enabled.

Deleting the backup-restore-test indices after stopping Operate completes within the existing RetryOperation budget of about 10 retries at 2 seconds each.

Index deletion in Elasticsearch becomes visible to the existence check after a bounded delay rather than indefinitely.
The failure on stable/8.8 is a timing-related error from the index-deletion poll, not an assertion failure in the backup or restore logic.
The failing run was triggered by an unrelated Renovate Docker tag bump (PR #60304), so the failure is not caused by that bump's contents.

Authorization records can be linked to a user directly, or indirectly through a group, role, or mapping rule the user belongs to, so the caller's own identities can be resolved to their effective grants.
Resolving the authenticated caller's identities into owner IDs yields only the caller's own identities, so clamping the owner scope to those IDs prevents exposure of other users' grants.

The StreamProcessor retries record writes with exponential backoff when the exporter backpressures the engine, introduced by #58058.
The backoff reset logic has been investigated and is correct, so the regression is not caused by a reset bug.
The current write-retry maximum delay is 50ms and lowering it to 10ms is acceptable for the exporter backpressure scenario.
ExponentialBackoff uses a private default backoff factor of 1.6 that is shared by every 2-arg ExponentialBackoffRetryDelay constructor.

Existing callers such as ClusterConfigurationManagerImpl, RepositoryNodeIdProvider and existing tests rely on the 2-arg constructors using the 1.6 factor, so they are unaffected by a new 3-arg overload.
A 3-arg constructor accepting a backoff factor can be added to ExponentialBackoff and ExponentialBackoffRetryDelay without breaking existing call sites.

By default grpc-java only schedules keepalive PINGs while at least one RPC call is active on the channel.

assumptions.target: pynput keyboard Listener on GNOME X11
assumptions.claim: The pynput keyboard Listener receives no physical key press or release events on mutter-based X11 sessions, because XRecord device_events never deliver them, even though the listener reports a successful start.

The evdev backend reads kernel input devices directly and supports X11 sessions, so it can be selected as the preferred hotkey backend when XDG_SESSION_TYPE is x11 and XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP contains GNOME.
The /dev/input device nodes are readable by the user when evdev is in use, and pynput remains a usable fallback when they are not.
Running the ibus engine command applies the engine's XKB map server-wide, and on GNOME this collapses a multi-layout keyboard map (such as us,de) down to a single layout.
stop() can re-read the live IBus engine after stop_engine_process() returns, and that reading reliably indicates whether a real engine is currently active.
The restore write still runs when teardown leaves Vocalinux selected as the engine or leaves no engine active, so the behaviour required by #558 is preserved.
The reported environment is gnome-shell 48.7 on Debian 13 running as an AppImage, and the fix is validated against that combination.
The job currently skips itself when FLATPAK_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY or FLATPAK_REPO_TOKEN is unset, and it does so by design.

The publish-aur job skips when its credentials are unset and does not fail the release run in that case.
A skipped publish-flatpak-remote job must not fail the release, so an unconfigured optional channel does not block a tag.
Any token with Contents write permission on VocaHQ/vocalinux-flatpak is accepted, and a fine-grained PAT is the recommended minimum.
The Flatpak remote is live, serves a signed OSTree repo via GitHub Pages, and has v0.18.2 published to it.
No Python code is changed by this PR, so no test additions or local test runs are needed for the change.
The function currently uses a bare lstrip() that strips all whitespace including newlines, destroying the leading \n produced by line-break commands.
Punctuated transcripts such as "New line." currently fail to match unpunctuated exact command matches and fall through to generic substitution, retaining the trailing period.
The function currently treats whitespace-only text as empty and returns early, discarding a \n before any backend runs.
Backends such as xdotool type a \n character as a Return keypress, so whitespace-only input can be passed to them verbatim.
Segments consisting only of spaces or tabs are stripped upstream during normalization and never reach inject_text.
The whisper.cpp backend emits punctuated transcripts such as "New line." with trailing periods for standalone voice commands.

assumptions.target: live KDE/X11 fake-mic dictation through whisper.cpp into xdotool
assumptions.claim: The end-to-end dictation setup on a live KDE/X11 system with fake microphone input is reproducible and was used to verify the fix.
The manylinux PyPI wheel for pywhispercpp bundles a libggml-cpu compiled with AVX2 and FMA instructions, which is why it crashes with SIGILL on pre-Haswell CPUs.
Setting GGML_SSE42, GGML_AVX, GGML_AVX2, GGML_BMI2, GGML_FMA and GGML_F16C to OFF yields a libggml-cpu containing zero VEX-encoded instructions, a true x86-64 baseline.
With GGML_NATIVE enabled (the default), ggml turns every GGML_* SIMD option on, so setting GGML_NATIVE=OFF alone does not remove -mavx2 and -mfma from the build.
Setting PIP_NO_BINARY=pywhispercpp makes pip build pywhispercpp from the hash-pinned sdist instead of installing the prebuilt wheel.
The snap part's build-environment can carry CMAKE_ARGS that are honoured when pip builds pywhispercpp from source.
The Flatpak module already defines CMAKE_ARGS and runs the pywhispercpp sdist build, so extra ISA flags can be appended to it.
The vendored wheel-bundled shared libraries keep their filenames and NEEDED entries, so swapping in a rebuilt libggml-cpu under the same name still resolves at load time.

The evdev keyboard backend currently only reads keyboard events and never grabs the input device, so the dictation shortcut is also delivered to the focused application.

Virtual devices (our own clones, ydotool, remappers) identify themselves with BUS_VIRTUAL, so filtering on that bustype reliably excludes them from being opened or grabbed.
Physical key repeat arrives as EV_KEY events with value 2 and can be forwarded verbatim, while EV_REP is stripped from the clone so autorepeat is not generated twice.

Permissions.from_str currently strips a trailing 11th character only when it is "+" or "@", and fails on any other 11th-character marker such as ".".
parse_ls_la passes the raw mode field (parts[0]) from ls -la output directly to Permissions.from_str without removing any marker itself.
On SELinux-enabled hosts, GNU coreutils ls appends "." as an 11th character to the mode field in ls -la output.
SandboxSession.ls() currently raises ValueError on SELinux-enabled hosts because of the unrecognized trailing marker.
The only trailing 11th-character markers that need handling are "+", "@", and "."; no other alternate-access marker appears in the ls output the sandbox consumes.
Existing tests cover the "+" and "@" marker cases and do not exercise a "."-suffixed mode string.
The exclude list is built by iterating sorted skip paths and emitting a `--exclude` argument for each relative path, and these excludes are passed to `tar` when persisting the workspace.
The current code uses `str.lstrip("./")`, which strips any leading run of '.' and '/' characters rather than a literal `./` prefix, causing dot-prefixed paths like `.venv` to lose their leading dot.
Dot-prefixed skip paths (e.g. `.venv`, `.git`, `.env`) reach the persistence step via `register_persist_workspace_skip_path` or ephemeral manifest entries and are therefore present in the skip set.
The Cloudflare backend already builds its workspace exclude paths with `removeprefix("./")`, so it correctly strips only a literal `./` prefix.
`tar` matches `--exclude ./venv` literally against archive member names and does not match the real `./.venv` directory, so the dot directory is currently included in the tar.

Passing a keyword named model_config to create_model() is interpreted by Pydantic as the model's configuration dict rather than as a field, causing the TypeError.
function_schema() builds the argument model via create_model(f"{name}_args", __base__=BaseModel, **fields), so any parameter name is passed directly as a keyword argument.
Other reserved names such as model_dump, model_validate and leading-underscore names already produce readable Pydantic errors, so model_config is the only one currently failing opaquely.
UserError is available in the codebase and is an appropriate exception type to raise for an invalid tool parameter name.

Calling rm on the workspace root path (".", "", "sub/..", or the absolute root) currently succeeds and deletes the entire workspace root.

The Unix local backend implements rm via shutil.rmtree on the host path, which removes the workspace root directory when given the root.
WorkspaceArchiveWriteError exists and accepts a context dict so it can carry a reason such as workspace_root_removal_refused.
The policy object exposes a sandbox_root() method returning the sandbox root path used for comparison.

Existing tests do not require rm of the workspace root to succeed, so refusing it will not break intended behaviour.

assumptions.target: safeClone copies in the six plugins
assumptions.claim: Each of the six plugins (Cline, OMO, Oh My Pi, OpenClaw, Pi, Prime) currently has an identical safeClone implementation kept in sync with its embedded twin under cli/beacon/internal/endpoint/hooks/assets/.
safeClone is the serializer that copies live hook payloads before they are sent to beacon-hooks.
OpenCode does not serialize hook payloads with safeClone and therefore needs no copy of it.
The file plugins/shared/safe-clone.ts exists and holds the single source definition of safeClone and maxDepth.
Each plugin can rely on the sync script in plugins/shared rewriting copies from the source, and the plugin bun run check failing when a copy diverges from it.
Bun is available to run the sync and check scripts and the TypeScript plugin sources.
The OpenClaw safeClone copy is plain JavaScript that the sync derives from the TypeScript source by exact line rewrites of its two type annotations, and that source matches those annotations.
CI runs the plugins/shared check and tests, so drift between copies and the source is caught on every change.
The queue previously dropped a batch after 6 failed send attempts, so telemetry captured during a long collector outage was lost.
MV3 clamps chrome.alarms periods to roughly 30 seconds, so the retry alarm cannot fire more often than that.
chrome.storage.local has a 10 MiB quota that the queue must stay within.
A browser restart or extension update can clear the retry alarm, so the queue must be flushed on service worker start.
The collector follows OTLP/HTTP retry rules: 429, 502, 503, 504, network errors and timeouts are retryable, and other non-2xx statuses mean the batch will never be accepted.
Queued batches are ordered by capture time and each batch's envelopes can be measured in bytes to enforce the 6 MiB cap.
The README currently states the queue guarantees eventual delivery, which this change must correct because retention is bounded.
A plain hermes process resolves its home directory via _apply_profile_override over get_default_hermes_root, following HERMES_HOME, the active_profile file, and profiles/<name> directories.
HERMES_HOME may be set in the environment and is honoured by Hermes when present, taking precedence over the ~/.hermes default.
HERMES_DATA_DIR_SUFFIX, when set, is appended to the default Hermes root (~/.hermes or %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes) to form the data directory.
A file named active_profile under the Hermes root holds the name of the sticky profile set by hermes profile use.
Each non-default profile lives in a directory profiles/<name> under the Hermes root that must exist for the profile to be usable.
Hermes treats profile names case-insensitively, maps default to the root, rejects reserved names, and requires names to match the profile-name regex.
Hermes reads its configuration and hooks from config.yaml inside the resolved home directory, so writes to any other location are never read by Hermes.
When a hook runs out of its budget (3s for post-commit and post-rewrite, 10s for pre-push) it currently gives up silently without recording anything.
A post-commit hook that exceeds its budget leaves the commit unlinked.
gitlink.HookRun exists and can measure a hook run's elapsed time per phase and count git processes spawned, at the cost of a clock read per step and an atomic add per git spawn.
gitShareAfterContext derives from context.WithoutCancel, so cancellation of the parent context does not propagate to spawned git processes.

assumptions.target: runtime log and its rotated archives
assumptions.claim: The runtime log and its rotated archives are readable and contain prior git.hook_budget_exceeded events that can be aggregated over a seven-day window.
The hook budgets are currently 3s for post-commit and post-rewrite and 10s for pre-push, and this change leaves them unchanged.
The Go standard library context package provides WithoutCancel, which is available in the toolchain this repository builds with.
On a privacy mode change, Connect currently deletes the staged cloud-backfill.jsonl before restaging, freeing its inode for reuse by the new temp file.
StageBackfill writes the new-mode backfill to a temp file and renames it over the existing cloud-backfill.jsonl, so the old copy is replaced atomically.
The beacon_backfill forwarder fingerprints staged backfill files by inode, so every restage must produce a file with a distinct inode to be shipped.
Freed inodes can be immediately reassigned to a newly created temp file, which is why deleting the old staged copy before restaging can yield the same inode.
The test's os.SameFile assertion is valid and will hold once the old copy is no longer deleted before restaging, and the test was previously failing only intermittently under parallel load.
The linux-test CI job runs the backfill tests and is currently blocked by this flaky test failing on unrelated PRs.
The repository (or its organization) has an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret configured by a repo admin before the new workflows run.
Cursor Bugbot is currently the only automated reviewer on PRs in this repo and will keep running unchanged alongside the new workflows.
The built-in GITHUB_TOKEN has sufficient permissions to post inline and summary comments on pull requests, so no GitHub App installation is required.
The anthropics/claude-code-action v1 release is available and supports running a PR review on pull_request events.
The anthropics/claude-code-security-review action is available and can be pinned to a specific commit SHA.

The Go modules currently pin a golang.org/x/text version with a published security advisory, and the bump target version is the first patched release.

When every rule is skipped, the scan currently reports the misleading message 'no rules to run (store is empty and baseline missing)' instead of naming the skipped rules.
The /api/findings endpoint currently does not return the skip list, so the dashboard cannot inform the user which rules need an upgrade.
The /api/findings endpoint returns HTTP 400 with a JSON body containing an error field when every rule is skipped.
Rule files declare their spec version as a threat-rules/vN identifier, such as threat-rules/v1.1 or threat-rules/v2.
PR #703 has already merged to the main branch without the follow-up push that this change is meant to include.
The 'Misleading error after all rules skip' edge case was acknowledged as a real issue in the Cursor Bugbot review thread on #703.

The rules loader currently has no spec version concept and aborts the whole rules directory when any rule uses a field the binary does not recognise.

Setting correlation.order to any permits its steps to match in any sequence, while the absent or sequence value preserves the existing ordered matching.

launchd refuses to bootstrap a plist located on an external volume (/Volumes/<disk>) with Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error, while the same plist works when copied to the startup volume.
A failed launchctl bootstrap currently causes the install to roll back its changes instead of continuing in a degraded state.

The user's home directory and ~/Library/LaunchAgents are on an external volume distinct from /Users in the affected configuration, and the startup volume is a different volume that is reachable at install time.

Returns a nil OTLP runtime list for a hook-only selection, and this nil value is what drives the fix.
Treats a nil Harnesses value as unspecified and falls back to default OTLP configuration, which is the path being changed so an explicit selection with no OTLP runtime configures nothing.

The system-mode collector already holds 127.0.0.1:13133 for its health-check extension when a user-mode install runs on the same Mac.
The user-mode collector's health-check extension binds a fixed 127.0.0.1:13133 unless a different port is configured.
Preflight checks only the OTLP gRPC and HTTP ports and does not check the health-check port, so a health-port conflict passes preflight.
A collector that exits before becoming ready currently surfaces only the generic 'Collector ports are not listening' error, with the real cause visible only in the collector's stderr log file.
Configs written before this change have no collector.health_port field, and such a missing field means the health-check port is 13133.
The user-mode collector writes its stderr to this log path, where the last error line can be read.
Extension API calls in the source currently use the chrome.* namespace and rely on it returning promises, so a browser.* / chrome.* shim can route them.
The existing build copies a single src/manifest.json into dist/ with no transform, and dist/ is the Chrome output directory.
On a Firefox install with host permissions withheld, the extension silently captures nothing and gives no indication that access is missing.
src/manifest.json is a single MV3 manifest using a service_worker background, and dist/manifest.json is byte-identical to it for the Chrome build.
Each build target is defined by an output directory, an esbuild target, and a manifest transform where null means copy the manifest verbatim.
Mozilla's web-ext CLI is available so that web-ext lint can run with warnings treated as errors in CI.
The existing end-to-end test suite passes unchanged against the Chrome build after the refactor.

These three packages fail on Windows due to a real product defect rather than a test assumption, so they are deliberately excluded from the Windows gate.

testenv.SetHome exists and sets HOME on all platforms, plus USERPROFILE, APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA on Windows.
testenv.HasPOSIXFileModes exists and returns false on Windows and true on Linux and macOS.

Records written by older releases may contain the legacy "noul" placeholder in the reason field.
The sync command writes its emitted events directly into the runtime log, which the runtime rotates at 10 MiB and keeps five archives of.
Log rotation deletes the oldest archive files once the retained archive count is exceeded, so events in those files become unrecoverable.
Per-session cursors advance after events are written, independent of whether those events survive rotation.
The sync summary reports an errors count and exit code that currently show success even when events were rotated out.
A --rotate-bytes flag is available to set the rotation size threshold for a single sweep.
Hooks and the collector can rotate the runtime log concurrently while a sweep is running.
The 60,300-event local history reproduces the reported loss on main, and the sweep is expected to reach the stated retention figures on the same history.
DeepSeek Harness runs hook commands inside the session sandbox, which in read-only and workspace-write modes cannot write outside the workspace.
Hook writes to ~/.beacon/endpoint/logs/runtime.jsonl currently fail under the default read-only sandbox and the hook still exits 0.
Running beacon endpoint dsh sync writes poll events under the deepseek_harness name into the same runtime log.
The doctor check harness_observed reports green whenever poll events exist, regardless of whether live hook capture is working.
reportEndpointWriteFailure in cli/beacon-h exists and can be extended to print the NOT recorded message to stderr with path and error.
The DeepSeek Harness sandbox modes are read-only (default), workspace-write, and danger-full-access, and the last is the only mode that permits outside writes.

assumptions.target: output selection with wantedList and excludedList
assumptions.claim: The current output filter treats a wantedList whose entries are all removed by excludedList as selecting every other list instead of nothing.

The MRS writer currently ignores errors from compression flush and file close and reports success regardless.

When excludedList removes every entry in wantedList, the exporter currently falls back to exporting unrelated lists instead of selecting nothing.
The existing container iterator streams values from a goroutine over the live map, so concurrent removal during iteration can race map traversal and leave producer goroutines blocked.
The current CIDR lookup does not normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses or prefix lengths, so queries such as ::ffff:192.0.2.0/120 fail to match 192.0.2.0/24.
Mapped prefixes shorter than /96 are valid input that the lookup path must be able to receive and reject explicitly.
The current MRS converter mishandles IPv6 ranges whose endpoints look like IPv4-mapped addresses, such as ::/80, and may drop them.
The current MRS converter accepts reversed ranges (start greater than end) without error, producing silent data loss.
The current MRS reader allocates buffers sized from untrusted length fields rather than streaming reserved bytes.
The current MRS writer discards compression-finalization errors instead of propagating them to the caller.
Loop() currently ranges over c.entries in a background goroutine, so consumers mutating the map concurrently can trigger a concurrent map iteration and write fatal error.
The cutter plugin calls container.Remove(entry, CaseRemoveEntry) from inside a range over container.Loop(), mutating the same map being iterated.
The fallthrough in Input() calls appendIPOrCIDR even when ipOrCIDR is empty, creating an empty entry that bypasses the wantedList filter.
Output converters currently fail with 'entry X has no prefix' when an empty entry is present in the container, rather than producing 'no entry is generated'.
walkLocalFile and walkRemoteFile apply the wantedList filter consistently and are the correct reference behaviour for the text input plugin.
Lookup() unmaps the query address to classify it as IPv4 but passes the original IPv4-mapped prefix to the IPv4 search, so mapped CIDRs are never matched.
Loop() can be changed to fill a fully buffered channel synchronously from a snapshot and close it before returning, without callers depending on a goroutine.
Each of the three bugs was reproduced before the fix was applied.
netip.ParsePrefix accepts IPv4-mapped IPv6 CIDR strings such as "::ffff:192.168.1.0/120" and returns a prefix whose Addr reports Is4In6 as true.
Prefixes inserted into the internal IP sets are currently stored as IPv6 prefixes without conversion when they are IPv4-mapped, which is why membership lookups for IPv4 addresses fail.
A mapped prefix with bit length of at least 96 maps to an IPv4 prefix whose length is the IPv6 bit length minus 96, so /120 becomes /24.
Mapped prefixes whose length is shorter than 96 bits describe an impossible IPv4 range and must be rejected rather than converted.
The internal IP sets store IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes in separate structures, so an IPv4 prefix inserted after normalization is found by IPv4 address lookups.
Addr.Unmap and Prefix.Masked are available in the Go standard library version used by the project to perform the conversion.
The existing tests for IP set lookups pass before this change and no existing test expects mapped IPv6 prefixes to remain as IPv6 entries.
